propositions: writes are keyed on (target_id, relation) allowing one pair to hold multiple relations, but removal is pair-scoped and returns only the most-recent link, creating asymmetry

when a pair holds two relations and a peer deletion targets one, the inbound reconciler declines with a permanent guard G5 if the net-active relation differs from the vanished one, preventing convergence
the pair-scoped unlink produces non-convergence on every pass because the removal record re-emits and G5 re-declines it, leaving only a log-visible non-convergence with no operator signal

the outbound differ dedupes direction-agnostically on vendor_type (not relation), so when a local dep collides with a same-vendor-type remote link in the opposite direction, the outbound ADD is skipped and G5 is reached
relation-scoped removal keyed on (target_id, relation) and symmetric with add_dependency will make G5 converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation instead of declining
CLI unlink gains optional relation argument with no-relation behavior backward-compatible to pair-scoped most-recent
